question: Should ClawHub repair this TypeScript 7 dependency branch now, or defer the major compiler upgrade until the verifier and lockfile compatibility work is planned?
rationale: The current branch is mechanically small but crosses a compiler API boundary and a supply-chain lockfile boundary, so accepting the upgrade requires maintainer ownership of the toolchain direction rather than a normal dependency-automerge decision.

options.title: Repair before merge
options.body: Update the verifier or dependency layout for TypeScript 7, restore the unrelated design-system integrity entry, and require the full type/package gates to pass before merge.

options.title: Defer the major bump
options.body: Ask Dependabot to ignore or recreate this major version later while keeping TypeScript 6.0.3 as the JavaScript compiler API dependency for now.

options.title: Accept the upgrade risk
options.body: Merge despite the broken gate and lockfile weakening, which would leave main requiring immediate follow-up repair.

recommendation.title: Repair before merge
recommendation.body: Update the verifier or dependency layout for TypeScript 7, restore the unrelated design-system integrity entry, and require the full type/package gates to pass before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete most recently touched the TypeScript/native dependency area that this PR is trying to reconcile.
